title: Declare and clear shared memory
starter:
let shared_lines (ty : string) (name : string) (n : int) : string list =
  []
hints: Return three strings: the declaration, the clearing loop, the barrier. Copy the punctuation from the listing above.
The loop's counter is always `z_`. It starts at `threadIdx.x`, stops below the array's size and steps by `blockDim.x`.
The middle line is `Printf.sprintf "for (int32_t z_ = threadIdx.x; z_ < %d; z_ += blockDim.x) %s[z_] = 0;" n name`.
explain: Three lines, in this order. The first declares the array as `__shared__`, so the block's threads all see the same one. The second is run by every thread: each starts at its own number and steps by the block size, so the threads split the clearing between them and no two clear the same element. The third is a barrier, so no thread reads the array before every element is zero.
